executive_summary: Today's intelligence picture is dominated by a significant escalation in Iranian-backed aggression, with the coordinated missile and drone strike on U.S. bases in Jordan killing two service members and leaving one missing, representing the most consequential direct attack on American forces in the current regional conflict cycle. The military and intelligence sections reinforce each other on this point, indicating the threat picture is assessed as escalating rather than episodic, suggesting Iran or its proxies may be probing for the threshold of U.S. retaliation tolerance. Separately, the domestic military environment reflects unrelated but concurrent institutional stressors, with a non-combat fatality at Vandenberg and a serious criminal case involving on-base neglect at Fort Benning signaling ongoing force readiness and welfare concerns that command attention even as operational focus shifts to the Middle East. The convergence of an active external threat from Iranian-aligned forces with internal personnel and discipline issues underscores the demand placed on military leadership to manage simultaneous crises across very different domains.

sections.title: Military
sections.intro: A direct Iranian strike killing two U.S. troops in Jordan marks a significant escalation in regional hostilities, dominating today's military picture.

items.headline: Iran kills two U.S. service members, one missing, in coordinated missile and drone strike on Jordan bases
items.summary: Iranian ballistic missiles and drones struck multiple U.S. and partner force positions in Jordan on Friday, killing two service members and leaving one unaccounted for. This represents one of the most direct and lethal Iranian attacks on American forces in the current Middle East crisis, raising immediate questions about U.S. rules of engagement and retaliatory posture. Watch for a White House and Pentagon response in the coming hours that could signal whether this triggers a broader military exchange.

items.headline: Space Force identifies airman killed in equipment accident at Vandenberg Space Force Base
items.summary: Airman 1st Class Cedric Eneluna died Thursday after the heavy machinery he was operating rolled off an embankment at Vandenberg Space Force Base in California. The incident underscores ongoing occupational safety risks in non-combat military environments. An investigation is expected to determine whether equipment maintenance or operator protocols contributed to the fatality.

items.headline: Fort Benning soldier and girlfriend charged with murder after infant and dogs starve to death in on-base housing
items.summary: A U.S. Army soldier and his girlfriend face murder charges after authorities found that their baby and three dogs had been starved to death in family housing at Fort Benning. The case raises serious concerns about oversight mechanisms for dependent welfare on military installations. It is likely to prompt renewed scrutiny of reporting protocols and social support services available to service members with dependents.

sections.title: Intel / OSINT
sections.intro: Today's intelligence picture is thin on distinct OSINT-category signals, with the most operationally significant open-source development being the Iranian-linked strike on a U.S. military installation in Jordan.

items.headline: Iranian-Backed Strike Kills Two U.S. Soldiers at Jordan Base, Escalating Regional Threat Picture
items.summary: A barrage attributed to Iranian-backed forces struck a U.S. base in Jordan, killing at least two American troops — a significant escalation in the pattern of proxy attacks on U.S. forces across the Middle East. Muwaffaq Salti Air Base hosts the largest concentration of U.S. tactical airpower in the region, making it a high-value target whose vulnerability has now been demonstrated publicly. Watch for U.S. attribution statements, retaliatory strike options being surfaced, and whether Iran moves to publicly distance itself from the attacking group.
